_comment: A routed squadron at the edge of its pursuer's reach keeps one couple() anchor instead of switching it every tick or two (#1801). A brittle player squadron (16 Cavalry at morale 0.5) stands on open ground; an enemy Infantry block (40 men, 10 files) 210 wu to its east, facing it, charges it with no player input. Measured 2026-11-06 on 40b48e39 against main a37af5c0, seed 0: the squadron turns to meet it and fights from tick 226, routs at tick 325 still in contact (326 on main), and flees north with the infantry following at the edge of melee range. Its physical contact flag flips 4 times over ticks 420 to 455 (none on main), and its anchor's speed changes by 0.013 wu a tick on average over ticks 420 to 470 (0.009 on main). Its men's centroid has moved 64.5 wu 150 ticks after the rout and 337.2 wu after 300 (63.3 and 323.7 on main). It is still fleeing north when the clip ends at tick 560 and rallies at tick 686 (687 on main). When the #1801 fix was made the anchor flipped with the contact flag, changing speed by 0.55 wu a tick on average over ticks 420 to 470 on main a58c122e against 0.08 on the fix 45a9bb85, and the position checks at ticks 430 to 448 pinned where the fix's anchor stood then (9.5, 9.5, 10.2 and 7.5 wu from main a58c122e's). Re-pinned with Ezra's approval on 2026-11-06, for #1915, where a troop whose combat wheel falls more than 75 degrees behind an enemy among its ranks keeps wheeling instead of turning in place. The infantry's centre stands 24.5 to 29.6 wu from the squadron's anchor, inside its own footprint, so the bearing to it runs away faster than the wheel can turn: the heading trails it by 34 to 138 degrees over ticks 276 to 326 and passes 75 degrees at tick 287. On main the squadron turned in place there; its contact flag dropped at tick 302 (301 or 302 on seeds 1 to 4), one morale step was missed, and it routed at tick 326 (302 on seed 2). Now it loses contact only at tick 228, just after first meeting the infantry, its morale reaches 0 at tick 324, and it routs at tick 325 still in contact on seeds 0 to 4. So the setup checks read ROUTING at 325 and 326 and in contact at 326. The four anchor-position checks at ticks 430 to 448 already fail on main a37af5c0 (the anchor 27.9 wu off at tick 430) and still do here (26.6 wu); that regression is #1913, and those pins are left as they are.

shape_residual.reason: The infantry pursuer (uid 1) deforms while it follows the router at the edge of melee range: shape_residual worst 37.1 against the 13.5 threshold on this clip's own declared ticks, from about tick 440 to the clip's end. The deformation is pre-existing (36.0 on main 45a9bb85 on the same samples), and the fix shifts it a little: the router's anchor no longer switches back and forth, which changes how the router, and so its pursuer, moves. Tracked as #1824.
